concepts.heading: Why a Little Checking Helps
concepts.plain: Most people are who they say they are. A few quick checks protect you from the few who are not.

concepts.heading: Make Sure They Are Real
concepts.plain: A short video call is the quickest way to know the person matches their photos.

concepts.heading: Warning Signs in Messages
concepts.plain: Rushing you, refusing video, or any talk of money are reasons to slow down or stop.

concepts.heading: Trust Your Gut
concepts.plain: You do not need proof to say no. A bad feeling is enough of a reason.

checks.prompt: Your new connection won't video call but asks for a loan for a plane ticket to meet you. What fits best?
options: Send a small amount to show good faith
Send it if they promise to pay you back
Stop and don't send money; this matches a common scam
checks.explanation: Refusing video and then asking for money is the classic pattern of a romance scam. Do not send money to someone you have not met.

checks.prompt: You feel uneasy about someone but can't say why. What does this lesson suggest?
options: Treat the feeling as a reason to slow down or stop
Ignore it unless you can prove something is wrong
Meet anyway so you don't seem rude
checks.explanation: Your unease is information. You can slow down or step away without proving anything.

a17c16fd-6a1e-5259-9692-b6b167f63bc5.takeaway: A little checking before you meet keeps the fun part fun.

concepts.heading: Pick a Public Place
concepts.plain: Meet somewhere busy, like a café or a park in daytime, not at anyone's home.

concepts.heading: Get There and Back on Your Own
concepts.plain: Use your own transport so you can leave whenever you want.

concepts.heading: Tell a Friend the Plan
concepts.plain: Share who, where and when with someone you trust, and agree a time to check in.

concepts.heading: Keep Some Things Private for Now
concepts.plain: Your home address, workplace and money details can wait until trust is built.

checks.prompt: Which plan keeps you most in control on a first meeting?
options: They pick you up from home so you don't have to drive
You meet at their place because it's quieter
You meet at a café, travel there yourself, and a friend knows the plan
checks.explanation: Your own transport, a public place and a friend who knows the plan mean you can leave at any time and someone knows where you are.

5b12fe43-d858-52bc-80c5-13a7ddc657e9.takeaway: Public place, your own way there and back, and a friend who knows the plan.

concepts.heading: Your Drink, Your Pace
concepts.plain: Keep your drink in sight and drink at a pace that keeps you clear-headed.

concepts.heading: Check In With Yourself
concepts.plain: Notice how you feel during the meeting, not just how they feel about you.

concepts.heading: It Is OK to Leave
concepts.plain: You never owe anyone more of your time. A short, polite line is enough.

concepts.heading: Signs of Pressure
concepts.plain: Pushing past a no, guilt trips and rushing you somewhere private are signs to leave.

checks.prompt: Halfway through a coffee, Sam feels pressured and wants to go. What should Sam do?
options: Say a short goodbye and leave; no big reason is needed
Stay until the end so it isn't awkward
Agree to go somewhere else to smooth things over
checks.explanation: You never owe anyone more time. A short, polite goodbye is enough.

checks.prompt: Your date says "I came all this way" when you say you'd like to end the evening. What is this?
options: A fair reason to stay longer
A guilt trip, which is a sign of pressure
A normal part of flirting
checks.explanation: Using guilt to get you to stay is a form of pressure. You can still leave.

7eb432ff-8164-58ce-8f55-3b97abf0b789.takeaway: You can leave at any point, for any reason.

concepts.heading: Check In With Your Friend
concepts.plain: Message your friend as agreed so they know you are safe.

concepts.heading: Be Honest About What's Next
concepts.plain: Say whether you'd like to meet again. A kind, clear no is better than silence.

concepts.heading: Block and Report
concepts.plain: If someone makes you feel unsafe, block them and report them so we can protect others.

concepts.heading: If Something Happened
concepts.plain: What happened is not your fault. Free, private help is available any time.

checks.prompt: You don't want to see someone again. Which is the kindest clear option?
options: Stop replying and hope they get the message
Keep chatting so they don't feel bad
Send a short, polite message saying you're not interested
checks.explanation: A short, honest message is clearer and kinder than silence, and you do not owe a long explanation.

checks.prompt: Someone pressured Priya on a date. What does this lesson say?
options: It was partly her fault for meeting them
It is not her fault, and free, confidential help is available
She should wait to see if it happens again before telling anyone
checks.explanation: Pressure or harm is the responsibility of the person who did it. Support is available any time.

5a1c071d-b382-5f16-b6ef-d5e322e619b0.takeaway: Check in, be honest, and use Block and Report when you need them.
